word-astronomy.t: My brother loves {astronomy} and owns a big telescope.
{Astronomy} is one of the oldest sciences.

word-theory.t: Scientists tested the {theory} with a new experiment.
That is an interesting {theory}, but I don't agree.

word-laboratory.t: The scientists work in a {laboratory} downtown.
Students must wear glasses in the {laboratory}.
The blood test results came back from the {lab}.

word-microscope.t: We looked at a drop of water under the {microscope}.
You need a {microscope} to see bacteria.
She got a small {microscope} for her birthday.

word-telescope.t: He pointed the {telescope} at the moon.
With a good {telescope}, you can see Saturn's rings.

word-atom.t: Everything around us is made of {atoms}.
A water molecule has two hydrogen {atoms}.
An {atom} is too small to see.

word-molecule.t: The {molecules} move faster when the water gets hot.
Scientists built a model of the {molecule}.

word-cell.t: Every living thing is made of at least one {cell}.
Red blood {cells} carry oxygen through the body.
The plant {cell} has a thick wall.

word-dna.t: You get half of your {DNA} from each parent.
The scientist studied the {DNA} of ancient animals.

word-evolution.t: We learned about the {evolution} of birds in class.
{Evolution} takes place over millions of years.
Darwin's book changed how people think about {evolution}.

word-species.t: Many {species} of birds live in this forest.
Scientists found a new {species} of frog.

word-chemical-element.t: Oxygen is the most common {element} in the Earth's crust.
Each {chemical element} has its own symbol.

word-hydrogen.t: Water is made of {hydrogen} and oxygen.

word-force.t: You need more {force} to open this heavy door.
Gravity is a {force} that pulls things down.
The {force} of the wind broke the fence.

word-gravity.t: The moon has less {gravity} than the Earth.

word-magnet.t: She put a {magnet} on the fridge.
A {magnet} picks up small pieces of iron.
The children played with a {magnet} in science class.

word-mass.t: The {mass} of the Earth is very large.
Weight depends on both {mass} and gravity.
Scientists measured the {mass} of the rock.

word-pressure.t: The {pressure} is lower on top of a mountain.
Deep under the sea, the water {pressure} is very high.

word-radiation.t: Doctors use {radiation} to treat some illnesses.
Workers wear special clothes to protect them from {radiation}.

word-nuclear.t: The country has a {nuclear} power plant.
Many people are afraid of {nuclear} weapons.
{Nuclear} energy does not produce much carbon.

word-solar-system.t: The Earth is part of our {solar system}.
There are eight planets in the {solar system}.
She drew a picture of the {solar system}.

word-galaxy.t: Our {galaxy} is called the Milky Way.
There are billions of stars in a {galaxy}.
They found a new {galaxy} very far away.

word-universe.t: The {universe} is very old and very big.
Some people think we are not alone in the {universe}.
Scientists are still learning how the {universe} began.

word-orbit.t: The Earth takes a year to complete its {orbit} around the sun.
The moon is in {orbit} around the Earth.

word-satellite.t: The {satellite} sends TV signals to our home.
The moon is a natural {satellite} of the Earth.

word-rocket.t: The {rocket} took off at six in the morning.
Thousands of people watched the {rocket} launch.
The {rocket} carried a satellite into space.

word-astronaut.t: My cousin wants to be an {astronaut}.
The {astronauts} lived on the space station for six months.
The {astronaut} waved before getting into the rocket.

word-comet.t: We saw a bright {comet} in the sky last night.
A {comet} has a long tail of ice and dust.
The {comet} comes close to Earth every 76 years.

word-asteroid.t: An {asteroid} hit the Earth millions of years ago.
Most {asteroids} are found between Mars and Jupiter.

word-black-hole.t: Nothing can escape from a {black hole}.
Scientists took the first picture of a {black hole}.
There is a huge {black hole} at the center of our galaxy.

word-mercury-planet.t: {Mercury} is the smallest planet in our solar system.
A year on {Mercury} is only 88 days.
It is hard to see {Mercury} because it is so close to the sun.

word-venus.t: You can often see {Venus} in the evening sky.
A day on {Venus} is longer than its year.

word-mars.t: Scientists want to send people to {Mars}.
{Mars} looks red because of the iron in its soil.
A robot is exploring {Mars} right now.

word-jupiter.t: {Jupiter} is bigger than all the other planets.
We looked at {Jupiter} through the telescope.

word-saturn.t: The rings of {Saturn} are made of ice and rock.
It takes {Saturn} about thirty years to go around the sun.

word-uranus.t: {Uranus} is very cold and far from the sun.

word-neptune.t: {Neptune} is the farthest planet from the sun.

word-fossil.t: The boy found a {fossil} on the beach.
This {fossil} is more than a hundred million years old.

word-dinosaur.t: The {dinosaurs} died out millions of years ago.
This museum has a huge {dinosaur} skeleton.

word-invention.t: Her latest {invention} saves water in the kitchen.
The printing press was a great {invention}.

word-discovery.t: The {discovery} of electricity changed the world.
The {discovery} of the old ship surprised everyone.

word-formula.t: The teacher wrote the {formula} on the board.
You can use this {formula} to find the area.

word-sample.t: We tested a {sample} of the river water.
The store gave out free {samples} of cheese.

word-observe.t: The children {observed} the ants for an hour.
Please {observe} what happens when we add water.

word-analyze.t: We need to {analyze} the results carefully.
She {analyzed} the data for her report.

word-chemical.t: A {chemical} reaction made the water change color.
Please do not mix these {chemical} products.

word-liquid.t: Don't carry {liquids} in your bag on the plane.

word-solid-matter.t: Ice is water in its {solid} form.
The baby is eating {solid} food now.
A {solid} keeps its shape when you put it in a bowl.

word-acid.t: Be careful, that {acid} can burn your skin.
The stomach uses {acid} to break down food.
